title: Degree-multiple affine standard-open refinement on any open of Proj
statement: Let $A=\bigoplus_{j\geq0}A_j$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring, $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj], $d\geq1$, and $U\subseteq P$ any open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. For every $x\in U$ and every open neighbourhood $N\subseteq U$ of $x$, there are $q\geq1$ and a homogeneous $g\in A_q$ such that $g^d\in A_{qd}$ and $x\in D_+(g^d)=D_+(g)\subseteq N\subseteq U$. This common standard open is affine, with its canonical scheme identification $D_+(g)=\operatorname{Spec}A_{(g)}$, where $A_{(g)}$ is the degree-zero part of $A_g$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. Consequently the family $\{D_+(f)\subseteq U:\ f\in A_{nd},\ n\geq1\}$, viewed as opens of $U$, is an affine-open basis of $U$. No quasi-compactness hypothesis on $U$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01MW (lemma-ample-on-proj), proof of clauses (6)--(7): standard opens form an affine basis, with positive powers to enforce a degree multiple; Tag 01MB (lemma-proj-scheme), affine standard opens.

proof.text: Identify $U$ with its open image in $P$ by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Since $N$ is open in the open subset $U$, it is open in $P$: write $N=U\cap V$ for an open $V\subseteq P$. Apply the positive-degree standard-open basis of [lem-sc-proj-standard-open-basis] to $x\in N$, obtaining $q\geq1$ and $g\in A_q$ with $x\in D_+(g)\subseteq N$.

source.place: Tag 00JP (lemma-topology-proj), (5); restriction of an open basis to an open subset

proof.text: The graded multiplication law gives $g^d\in A_{qd}$ by multiplying $d$ copies of $g$. For each point represented by a homogeneous prime $\mathfrak p$ of [def-pc-proj], one has $g^d\in\mathfrak p$ if and only if $g\in\mathfrak p$: the reverse implication is closure under multiplication, and the forward implication follows by induction from primality, since $d\geq1$. Thus $D_+(g^d)=D_+(g)$ as opens of $P$, so also as open subschemes with the restricted structure sheaf. The inclusions from Step 1 remain valid.

source.place: Tag 01MW (lemma-ample-on-proj), proof: positive powers preserve standard opens

proof.text: Apply [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open] to the positive-degree homogeneous $g\in A_q$. It gives the canonical scheme isomorphism $D_+(g)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A_{(g)})$, hence affineness of the common open of Step 2. This is the whole standard open contained in $U$, whose scheme structure is the restriction from $P$, rather than an arbitrary intersection of an affine open with $U$.

source.place: Tag 01MB (lemma-proj-scheme), affine identification of standard opens

proof.text: For the final family, every $f\in A_{nd}$ with $n\geq1$ has positive degree $nd$, so [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open] makes $D_+(f)$ affine. If it is contained in $U$, it is an open subscheme of $U$ by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Given any $x\in N\subseteq U$ as above, Steps 1--2 put $D_+(g^d)$ in this family with $n=q$, containing $x$ and contained in $N$. This is precisely the neighbourhood criterion for a basis on $U$. All choices were made for one neighbourhood at a time; no finite covering or quasi-compactness was used.

source.place: Tag 01MW (lemma-ample-on-proj), proof of (6)--(7), the standard-open basis argument

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q96-bf204b9eb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and every cited statement. The delivery is a one-level split with no new nodes. The statement, stmt_deps and source are unchanged, proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses, and there is no SGA citation. There is no repair note for this item. Sources checked: Stacks 00JP (2) and (5) (algebra.tex l.13450); 01MB (constructions.tex l.1267); 01MW (5)-(7) and its proof (l.1948-1990). In 01MW, quasi-compactness only serves to choose a common d. With d fixed in advance, the pointwise power argument needs no finiteness, so the statement is not weakened. Step 1: lem-sc-proj-standard-open-basis (reviewed PASS by J1) gives g in A_q with q at least 1 and x in D_+(g) inside N. Step 2: g^d is in p exactly when g is, by primality and d at least 1, so D_+(g^d)=D_+(g); this is genuinely elementary. Step 3: prop-nagata-proj-standard-open (Mathlib leaf, basicOpenIsoSpec) gives D_+(g) = Spec A_(g); its Proj, def-nagata-affine-proj, has the same Mathlib match, AlgebraicGeometry.Proj, as def-pc-proj. Step 4 is the neighbourhood criterion for a basis. Edge cases A=0, U empty, d=1, A=k[x] with deg x=2, a non-quasi-compact U and nilpotent f all hold. There is no cycle, since the basis lemma's proof uses only lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion (0) and def-nagata-affine-proj. A duplicate search of the DAG found no node stating the degree-multiple refinement, and the parent lem-trf-proj-twist-section-basic-open Step 3 uses exactly this statement. The tool use of lem-sc-proj-standard-open-basis is accepted: it is a generic Proj-topology fact used as a black box, and the unit sk-i-curve-zero route has no Proj step. No fixes.
